items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: *choke*
Countless Chirpers fall like raindrops, each playing a different voice.

items.speaker: Doctor?
items.text: I have a son your age. Maybe you two can play together when you're feeling better.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Uggh. No, no ...
Maxim flails outward, trying to catch the Chirpers as they fall, but each one passes through his fingers in vain.

items.speaker: Engineer?
items.text: This is a fine gadget, don't you think? Maybe we should install it in our robot's head.

items.speaker: Young Woman?
items.text: We're so very grateful. Thank you! Thank you for not abandoning us!

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: No, no, no, no!
One of the Chirpers reflects in the dark pools of his eyes.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Papa, Mama?

items.speaker: Rozaliya
items.text: Vanya, has our country survived?

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Yes, Mama. People are even growing flowers again. I picked your favorites. But I couldn't bring them to your funeral.

items.speaker: Rozaliya
items.text: Are you taking good care of yourself?

items.speaker: Rozaliya
items.text: What is life like now? Are the people happy?

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Life is ...

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: I wish I could see all the latest technology. What can robots do now?
Maxim buries his head in his hands, his voice muffled.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: It's all so wonderful, Papa, Mama. We stopped the Plague, and now we're going to explore the cosmos.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: And what of you, little Vanya? How have you contributed?

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Everything has gotten better. I wish you could see.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: We're just happy to know things are better now. Though I admit I am jealous of you.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Shouldn't you be angry? They're enjoying this world because of you, but they don't even know your names. They don't know what you gave up for them, what I lost for them!

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: Why should we be angry, son? All that we did was in the hopes that the future would be brighter for our people and for you.

items.speaker: Rozaliya
items.text: The future is yours now, Vanya. All we want is for you to make it a better place.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: Don't let us down.

items.speaker: Rozaliya
items.text: He won't. I know our little Vanya has grown into a good man.
The Chirper drops to the ground and disappears.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: No, no.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Mama, Papa, don't go.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They have to go, Maxim. That's just the way of things. But you can choose to let them inspire you instead of dragging you into despair.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Don't push too hard, Vertin. He needs time to process things.
Knees on the ground, Maxim bends over and cradles his head. His trembling fingers reach toward his temple.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: *crying* I want to go home.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Warning: Data overflow detected. This space may be compromised, comrade.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: She's right, Vertin. I'm reading a cortisol spike. You don't have much time before his brain activity shuts down!
Crack.
Crack. Crack.
Maxim's body begins to break apart. Streams of transparent fluid leak out from his forehead and then from everywhere else.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: I need to go home.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: His dream state might collapse at any moment! You need to get out of there!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Not without the password. Is there anything else we can do?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Absolutely not! Your safety is top priority! Find somewhere secure now! I'm dragging you out!

items.speaker: X
items.text: Wait. That fluid must be polymer. It might still have an imprint of his memories. It's our last chance!
There's a sudden burst of commotion from the huddle of survivors.
The leaking substance turns into a small flood, rising up to the ankles of the two intruders in his collapsing dream.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If these are his memories, then where's the password?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Did you hear me, Vertin? Get out!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Give me more time! I can still find it.
The rising fluid begins to cover the chest.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Comrade Doctor, you must leave. I will continue the mission.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What do you mean? How?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: My sensors and processing ability are more efficient than yours, comrade. I will have a higher chance of retrieving the password in the time we have left.
She generates an egg-shaped barrier to create a safe zone around her companion, parting the viscous fluid like the Red Sea.
She walks toward Maxim. The closer she gets, the higher the pressure on the barrier, causing its surface to crack.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Confirming Vertin's status. Operable! Disconnect!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Wait! Hold on, no!

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Damn, you actually made it. That's some good news at least.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: P-3? What are you doing here?

items.speaker: Right
items.text: We have disabled most of the facility's hostile robots, but we were unable to secure any vehicles suitable for an evacuation.

items.speaker: Right
items.text: Requesting synchronization.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Are you alright, Vertin?
Mesmer leans over to inspect her reckless colleague. X, meanwhile, is still nursing what looks to be an open-hand smack to his face—An unforeseen consequence of his suggestion.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm alright, Mesmer. But Left is still inside.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Before I got out, she ...

items.speaker: Right
items.text: Synchronization complete. Please allow me to provide help.
Right connects herself to the Artificial Somnambulism machine without hesitation.

items.speaker: Right
items.text: Warning: data ... overflow ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Left? Right?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: W-What are they doing?

items.speaker: X
items.text: I believe this is their method of sharing computational power. Though the ballet aesthetic only serves as a personal affectation of the designer.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Watch out!
The Twins lie on the ground in a disjointed heap. Their bodies are charred.
There are still sparks popping out of the interfaces along their spines.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Password and antidote composition secured.
As Left points at the control room's computer, the screen turns on and displays a message.

items.speaker: Broadcast
items.text: Self-destruct sequence terminated.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Phew ...
Mesmer leans back against the wall and allows herself to sink down to the ground, where she inadvertently presses on the muzzle of X's modified gun.
*click*
The familiar sweet melody begins to chime from it, playing over the exhausted assembly.
As it does, the Twins begin to stir.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What is it? Are you alright?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: That song ... My emotion module is experiencing a reaction to it.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: However, I am unable to discern the programming that explains this reaction.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Has my programming been corrupted, or do I remember it from somewhere?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Please, comrade. May I listen to it again?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's a beautiful song, isn't it? I suppose even a robot might find it touching.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Touching, yes. Added to database.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Something's irked me this entire time. If the Twins were able to access Artificial Somnambulism, that must mean they have a consciousness. Perhaps they can even dream.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Were we still within your Artificial Somnambulism, or was it only Limbo after all? Can I dream?

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: 'Course you can. Bots like you and Char-les gotta have feelings, right? Why else would he be such a pain in my ass?

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Seems like a question for another time, though. You two should get yourselves repaired. I don't want the boss to blame me for you ladies falling apart.

items.speaker: P-3
items.text: Damn. There is something familiar about that song, isn't there?
